passages.text: My brothers, as you hold out your faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, do not show favoritism.
passages.sermon:
James writes to Christians.
James calls them brothers.
James speaks to people who believe in Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ is our Lord.
Jesus Christ is glorious.
Do not show favoritism.
You must not mix faith in Jesus with favoritism.
passages.original: Ἀδελφοί μου μὴ ἐν προσωπολημψίαις ἔχετε τὴν πίστιν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῆς δόξης

passages.text: Suppose a man comes into your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor man in shabby clothes also comes in.
passages.sermon:
Suppose a meeting of believers gathers.
A man enters the meeting.
He wears a gold ring.
He wears fine clothes.
A poor man also enters.
The poor man wears shabby clothes.
passages.original: Ἐὰν γὰρ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς συναγωγὴν ὑμῶν ἀνὴρ χρυσοδακτύλιος ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ εἰσέλθῃ δὲ καὶ πτωχὸς ἐν ῥυπαρᾷ ἐσθῆτι

passages.text: If you lavish attention on the man in fine clothes and say, “Here is a seat of honor,” but say to the poor man, “You must stand” or “Sit at my feet,” have you not discriminated among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
passages.sermon:
You see a man wearing fine clothes.
You pay special attention to him.
You say to him, "Sit here in a good place."
You see a poor man.
You say to the poor man, "Stand over there."
Or you say to the poor man, "Sit at my feet."
Then you treat someone rich differently than someone who is poor.
Then you discriminate against the poor.
You discriminated against the poor with your actions because, in your heart, you first judged the poor.
And so you became a judge with evil thoughts.
We should not judge like this.
We should not discriminate like this.
passages.original: ἐπιβλέψητε δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν φοροῦντα τὴν ἐσθῆτα τὴν λαμπρὰν καὶ εἴπητε Σὺ κάθου ὧδε καλῶς καὶ τῷ πτωχῷ εἴπητε Σὺ στῆθι ἐκεῖ ἢ Κάθου ὑπὸ τὸ ὑποπόδιόν μου καὶ οὐ διεκρίθητε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἐγένεσθε κριταὶ διαλογισμῶν πονηρῶν

passages.text: Listen, my beloved brothers: Has not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom He promised those who love Him?
passages.sermon:
God chooses people.
God chooses people who are poor in this world.
God makes these chosen poor people rich in faith.
God gives these people the right to inherit His kingdom.
God promised this kingdom to those who love Him.
We need to listen to this.
We are beloved brothers of James.
passages.original: Ἀκούσατε ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί οὐχ ὁ Θεὸς ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πτωχοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ πλουσίους ἐν πίστει καὶ κληρονόμους τῆς βασιλείας ἧς ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: But you have dishonored the poor. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into court?
passages.sermon:
Those who have discriminated against the poor have dishonored the poor.
The rich are the ones oppress us.
The rich are the ones who drag us into court.
passages.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠτιμάσατε τὸν πτωχόν οὐχ οἱ πλούσιοι καταδυναστεύουσιν ὑμῶν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἕλκουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς κριτήρια

passages.text: Are they not the ones who blaspheme the noble name by which you have been called?
passages.sermon:
God called us by this His noble name.
But these rich people blaspheme God's noble name.
These rich people speak against the noble name.
passages.original: οὐκ αὐτοὶ βλασφημοῦσιν τὸ καλὸν ὄνομα τὸ ἐπικληθὲν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς

passages.text: If you really fulfill the royal law stated in Scripture, “Love your neighbor as yourself,” you are doing well.
passages.sermon:
God gave a royal law in Scripture.
This law says, “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
If you truly obey this law, then you do what is right.
You do well when you love others as you love yourself.
passages.original: Εἰ μέντοι νόμον τελεῖτε βασιλικὸν κατὰ τὴν γραφήν Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν καλῶς ποιεῖτε

passages.text: But if you show favoritism, you sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.
passages.sermon:
If you show favoritism, then you commit sin.
If you show favoritism, then the law convicts you as a transgressor.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ προσωπολημπτεῖτε ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζεσθε ἐλεγχόμενοι ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου ὡς παραβάται

passages.text: Whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles at just one point is guilty of breaking all of it.
passages.sermon:
A person may try to keep the whole law.
This person may obey every command.
But if this person fails at just one point, then he is guilty.
He is guilty of breaking all of the law.
passages.original: Ὅστις γὰρ ὅλον τὸν νόμον τηρήσῃ πταίσῃ δὲ ἐν ἑνί γέγονεν πάντων ἔνοχος

passages.text: For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” If you do not commit adultery, but do commit murder, you have become a lawbreaker.
passages.sermon:
God gave the law.
God says, "Do not commit adultery."
God also says, "Do not murder."
If you do not commit adultery, then you obey part of the law.
But if you murder, then you break the law.
If you break even one command, then you become a lawbreaker.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ εἰπών Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς εἶπεν καί Μὴ φονεύσῃς εἰ δὲ οὐ μοιχεύεις φονεύεις δέ γέγονας παραβάτης νόμου

passages.text: Speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom.
passages.sermon:
God's law gives freedom. You will be judged by this law.
Speak as someone who will be judged by this law.
Perform actions as someone who will be judged by this law.
passages.original: Οὕτως λαλεῖτε καὶ οὕτως ποιεῖτε ὡς διὰ νόμου ἐλευθερίας μέλλοντες κρίνεσθαι

passages.text: For judgment without mercy will be shown to anyone who has not been merciful. Mercy triumphs over judgment.
passages.sermon:
God will judge every person.
If someone has not been merciful, then God will not show mercy to them.
Mercy is greater than judgment.
Mercy wins over judgment.
passages.original: ἡ γὰρ κρίσις ἀνέλεος τῷ μὴ ποιήσαντι ἔλεος κατακαυχᾶται ἔλεος κρίσεως

passages.text: What good is it, my brothers, if someone claims to have faith, but has no deeds? Can such faith save him?
passages.sermon:
James calls us believers in Jesus his brothers.
Suppose someone claims to have faith.
But this person does not have works that live out their faith.
What good is claiming to have faith but lacking deeds?
Can faith without deeds save that person?
passages.original: Τί τὸ ὄφελος ἀδελφοί μου ἐὰν πίστιν λέγῃ τις ἔχειν ἔργα δὲ μὴ ἔχῃ μὴ δύναται ἡ πίστις σῶσαι αὐτόν

passages.text: Suppose a brother or sister is without clothes and daily food.
passages.sermon:
A brother or a sister may have no clothes.
A brother or a sister may lack daily food.
passages.original: ἐὰν ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἀδελφὴ γυμνοὶ ὑπάρχωσιν καὶ λειπόμενοι τῆς ἐφημέρου τροφῆς

passages.text: If one of you tells him, “Go in peace; stay warm and well fed,” but does not provide for his physical needs, what good is that?
passages.sermon:
Suppose you see a brother or sister who lacks clothes. 
This brother or sister also lacks daily food.
Suppose you say to them, "Go in peace."
And suppose you say, "Stay warm and be well fed."
Suppose you have food and clothes to give them.
But you do not give them what their body needs.
Then your words do not help them.
Your words are empty.
And your words do no good.
passages.original: εἴπῃ δέ τις αὐτοῖς ἐξ ὑμῶν Ὑπάγετε ἐν εἰρήνῃ θερμαίνεσθε καὶ χορτάζεσθε μὴ δῶτε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐπιτήδεια τοῦ σώματος τί τὸ ὄφελος

passages.text: So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.
passages.sermon:
Faith is trust in God.
Faith must produce action.
If faith does not produce action, then the faith is not alive.
If faith does not result in works, then the faith is dead.
Faith alone, without works, has no life.
passages.original: οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις ἐὰν μὴ ἔχῃ ἔργα νεκρά ἐστιν καθ’ ἑαυτήν

passages.text: But someone will say, “You have faith and I have deeds.” Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds.
passages.sermon:
James wrote this letter to Christians.
James taught about faith and actions.
Someone may say, “You have faith.”
Another may say, James has deeds.
Can someone show a true faith that is without deeds?
No! We prove our faith by our works.
passages.original: Ἀλλ’ ἐρεῖ τις Σὺ πίστιν ἔχεις κἀγὼ ἔργα ἔχω δεῖξόν μοι τὴν πίστιν σου χωρὶς τῶν ἔργων κἀγώ σοι δείξω ἐκ τῶν ἔργων μου τὴν πίστιν

passages.text: You believe that God is one. Good for you! Even the demons believe that—and shudder.
passages.sermon:
You believe that there is one God.
This belief is good.
However, demons also believe that God is one.
Demons tremble because of their belief in God.
passages.original: σὺ πιστεύεις ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν ὁ Θεός καλῶς ποιεῖς καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια πιστεύουσιν καὶ φρίσσουσιν

passages.text: O foolish man, do you want evidence that faith without deeds is worthless?
passages.sermon:
Faith without deeds is worthless.
A foolish person does not understand this.
Faith alone, without actions, has no value.
passages.original: Θέλεις δὲ γνῶναι ὦ ἄνθρωπε κενέ ὅτι ἡ πίστις χωρὶς τῶν ἔργων ἀργή ἐστιν

passages.text: Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
passages.sermon:
Abraham is our father in the faith.
Abraham had a son.
The name of the son of Abraham was Isaac.
Abraham offered his son on the altar.
God saw what Abraham did.
Abraham did a great work of obedience to God.
God justified Abraham because of the actions of Abraham.
Abraham was justified by what he did.
passages.original: Ἀβραὰμ ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη ἀνενέγκας Ἰσαὰκ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον

passages.text: You see that his faith was working with his actions, and his faith was perfected by what he did.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man of faith.
Abraham lived out his faith through his actions.
Abraham’s faith worked together with his actions.
Abraham’s actions showed his faith.
Abraham’s faith became complete through the deeds he did.
passages.original: βλέπεις ὅτι ἡ πίστις συνήργει τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ἡ πίστις ἐτελειώθη

passages.text: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.
passages.sermon:
Abraham believed God.
God counted Abraham’s belief as righteousness.
Scripture tells us this.
After Abraham believed God, when Abraham was tested, Abraham obeyed God.
And thus the Scripture was fulfilled through Abraham living out his faith.
And God called Abraham his friend.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπληρώθη ἡ γραφὴ ἡ λέγουσα Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην καὶ φίλος Θεοῦ ἐκλήθη

passages.text: As you can see, a man is justified by his deeds and not by faith alone.
passages.sermon:
A person is justified by his actions that come from his faith.
A faith that is without works does not justify a person.
Faith alone without deeds does not justify a person.
Actions coming from faith are necessary for justification.
passages.original: ὁρᾶτε ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος καὶ οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως μόνον

passages.text: In the same way, was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions when she welcomed the spies and sent them off on another route?
passages.sermon:
Rahab was a prostitute.
Rahab welcomed the Jewish spies.
Rahab hid and sent the spies by a different way so the leaders of Jericho would not kill the spies.
Rahab acted with courage and faith.
God justified Rahab because of her actions, which came from her faith.
Rahab was justified by what she did because of what she believed.
passages.original: Ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ῥαὰβ ἡ πόρνη οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη ὑποδεξαμένη τοὺς ἀγγέλους καὶ ἑτέρᾳ ὁδῷ ἐκβαλοῦσα

passages.text: As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.
passages.sermon:
A body without the spirit is dead.
And in the same way, faith without deeds is also dead.
passages.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα χωρὶς πνεύματος νεκρόν ἐστιν οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις χωρὶς ἔργων νεκρά ἐστιν
